# Does China Own Apple? With Patrick McGee

First listed: 2025-05-26 | Evaluation cutoff: 2026-11-10

[Back to library](../README.md)

## Source versions

- [YouTube: Does China Own Apple? With Patrick McGee](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=X3K6WaX1Chk) - 2025-05-26
- [Substack: Does China Own Apple? With Patrick McGee](https://realeismanplaybook.substack.com/p/does-china-own-apple-with-patrick-cc9) - 2025-06-05

Earliest listed publication among matched versions, not proof of an unedited contemporaneous archive. Claim timestamps refer to the reviewed version.

## Summary

McGee explains Apple’s China concentration as an incremental supplier migration reinforced by custom tooling, training and dense industrial networks. Eisman explicitly adopts several parts of the dependence and knowledge-transfer thesis. The review distinguishes genuine assembly relocation from full supply-chain independence. Primary records correct total-China production rhetoric, a long-lived-asset figure and the breadth of tariff relief. Apple’s services growth and Huawei’s local sales lead are supported, while political motives, private agreements and most causal innovation claims remain unresolved.

This is chiefly an industrial-history and geopolitical-risk interview, not a timed stock forecast. Its useful manufacturing distinctions survive, but absolute geography and relocation claims need qualification. Guest assertions are kept separate unless Eisman explicitly restates or endorses them. No stock-price outcome is used to prove the proposed geopolitical mechanism.

<a id="youtube-X3K6WaX1Chk-c005"></a>
### 005. Outsourcing converts some owned-factory fixed costs into manufacturing charges that vary with orders.

**Right** | Patrick McGee | analytical principle | major

[Source at 5:22-5:46](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=X3K6WaX1Chk&t=322s) | Stance: asserted | Horizon: not stated

The mechanism holds where contracts charge per unit without equivalent take-or-pay obligations; it does not guarantee total savings.

Qualification: Apple later retains substantial supplier tooling, so the entire production cost base is not purely variable.

Conditional reasoning: Owned-factory depreciation and staffing can remain when output falls. Replacing those obligations with a per-unit contract makes that portion of buyer cost equal to unit fee times ordered output. Fixed supplier commitments and retained tooling must be added separately.

Assessment test: Inspect commitments, tooling ownership and minimum volumes.

<a id="youtube-X3K6WaX1Chk-c037"></a>
### 037. Apple has earned about 80% of smartphone operating profits while shipping only about 20% of phones.

**Right** | Steve Eisman | material factual premise | major

[Source at 24:02-24:40](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=X3K6WaX1Chk&t=1442s) | Stance: asserted | Horizon: not stated

- [Q1 2023 global smartphone market](https://counterpointresearch.com/en/insights/global-smartphone-market-declines-14-yoy-q1-2023-apple-records-highest-ever-q1-share) (2023-05-05): The original market estimate puts Apple at 21% of shipments and nearly half of smartphone revenue in Q1 2023. The subsequent Q2 release reports Q1 Apple operating-profit share at 84%.
- [Apple smartphone revenue and operating profit, Q2 2023](https://counterpointresearch.com/de/insights/apples-smartphone-revenue-operating-profit-hit-june-quarter-records-q2-2023) (2023-08-04): The inspected primary release reports Apple at 85% of smartphone operating profit in Q2 2023, compared with 84% the preceding quarter and 81% a year earlier. These are industry estimates, not audited Apple segment profits.

The April electronics reciprocal-tariff exclusion did not repeal this distinct order.

<a id="youtube-X3K6WaX1Chk-c076"></a>
### 076. India can perform final assembly while remaining dependent on Chinese components and subassemblies.

**Right** | Patrick McGee | analytical principle | major

[Source at 41:56-42:33](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=X3K6WaX1Chk&t=2516s) | Stance: asserted | Horizon: not stated

Assembly location and upstream origin are logically separate; relocating the final stage does not by itself relocate prior production.

Qualification: This proves the distinction, not the claimed proportion of Indian iPhone value added originating in China.

Conditional reasoning: For a supply chain with component production in country A and final assembly in B, the finished item can be assembled in B while still requiring inputs from A. Changing only the final operation leaves the upstream dependency unchanged.

Assessment test: Determine actual upstream sourcing rather than infer it from the final label.


<a id="youtube-X3K6WaX1Chk-c077"></a>

**Mixed** | Patrick McGee | analytical principle | major

[Source at 42:09-42:31](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=X3K6WaX1Chk&t=2529s) | Stance: asserted | Horizon: not stated

Substantial transformation can determine origin, but simple final assembly is not automatically sufficient; CBP uses a fact-specific test and other tariffs may still apply.

Qualification: The statement should not be simplified into any final assembly avoids every tariff.

Assessment test: Inspect the actual iPhone process and binding origin ruling, then apply all tariff schedules.

- [Country-of-origin determination and substantial-transformation analysis](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/FR-2025-04-03/html/2025-05733.htm) (2025-04-03): CBP states that minimal or simple assembly generally does not establish substantial transformation; complex meaningful operations may do so under a case-specific totality-of-circumstances test. This is a general principle, not an iPhone-specific ruling.
- [Reciprocal tariff exclusion for specified electronics](https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/USDHSCBP/bulletins/3db9e55) (2025-04-11): HTS 8517.13.00 and other specified electronics were excluded from Executive Order 14257 reciprocal tariffs retroactive to April 5. The notice does not eliminate separately imposed China duties.

## Framework and tools

- Trace factory locations and process steps rather than supplier headquarters.
- Separate final assembly, component production and full ecosystem independence.
- Analyze path dependence and local supplier-network effects.
- Distinguish industrial design, product engineering and manufacturing engineering.
- Separate high profit share from proof of its cause.
- Distinguish known facts from inferred political motives and undisclosed agreements.
- Treat mutually profitable trade as compatible with strategic externalities.

Tools and charts discussed, not a complete visual inspection:

- Historical supplier and factory geography.
- Apple long-lived assets by country and supplier tooling.
- Smartphone shipment, revenue and operating-profit shares.
- Average selling prices and supplier margins.
- Final-assembly origin versus substantial-transformation rules.
- Huawei and Apple China market shares.
- Services revenue and product innovation comparisons.

## Source cautions

The introduction names Patrick McGee. Eisman asks questions and summarizes what he read; McGee gives the extended historical narrative. Explicit Eisman restatements are separately coded where material. Brief acknowledgments do not transfer all guest claims to Eisman. The final overlapping scale comment has medium attribution confidence.
- The opening montage repeats later material and is not the primary location for claims.
- Automatic captions distort names including Foxconn, Inventec, Quanta, Luxshare, Goertek, Wingtech, Jony Ive and Xi Jinping.
- The labor-problems absolute is immediately challenged and qualified; the corrected meaning is preserved.
- The episode explicitly distinguishes Indian final assembly from upstream Chinese manufacturing, which limits how its relocation rhetoric should be graded.
- The historical profit-share comparison has no exact year; the evidence verifies a matching historical example.
- The guest's $275 billion figure is a reported agreement, not independently inspected proof of incremental capital expenditure.
- The source was read through all 3,150 seconds including the final geopolitical discussion and disclaimer.
